D33·c12x — 2026-10-10
chose: 3.1 region leases, built as: a lanes run gives each lane session a PreToolUse hook (matcher Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit) through that session's own --settings file, running `sofar event lease` on the TypeScript engine only (sofar-core answers exit 64, as for drive-await; rust-core D15/D16 scoped, not superseded: the core owns no new shape). Leases are per-lane append-only files beside the lane locks, `<pool>/lane-<k>.lease.jsonl`: the coordinator writes the header (run, task, title, first assignment time, mode) when it assigns the lane and deletes the file when the job ends, after gate and landing; the hook appends claims and waits; a lease counts only while its lane lock is held. A region is the deepest markdown section or code symbol (indentation outline plus declaration patterns) holding the edit's old_string, its own lines or with its children; Write, NotebookEdit and other file types take the whole file; `.sofar/` and merge=union paths never lease. Two regions overlap on the same name, on an ancestor that holds its children, or on the whole file. The older task (first assignment in the run, then lane number) wins, so a session is steered or denied only by an older holder and the wait-for graph has no cycle. Steer is additionalContext with no permissionDecision, so the edit applies and r4-fixes D17 holds; `--leases deny` returns permissionDecision deny (D14); `--leases off` is 3.4's naive arm; default steer, a per-driver knob that is not recorded. A session that ends with no task change after a steer has parked: its handoff stays `stall` with detail `parked on a lease …`, is not counted toward --max-stalls, and its task is held out of the ready set until every holder's lease is gone, then its branch integrates the base before the relaunch.
over: Widening the project PreToolUse matcher (every interactive edit of every sofar user would pay a hook spawn, a node boot where no native core is installed). Porting the lease logic to sofar-core too (two implementations of a driven-only path). Leases as record events (an event per edit, for state that is machine-local coordination; cloud lanes cannot read it either, 4.3). Line-range regions (each lane edits its own copy, so line ranges drift while names hold). A new `parked` handoff reason (a schema change while packages/schema/src is mid-edit by a peer session). First holder wins (two lanes each parked on the other's region livelock).
because: Only a driven lane can collide with another lane, so only a lane session should pay for the check, and the driver already writes each session's settings file (2.4, D8). Files beside the lane locks need no fold and no record read on the edit path, and the lock tells a dead driver's leftover lease from a live one. Names are what two copies of a file share. Wound-wait ordering is what makes "older task wins" a no-deadlock guarantee rather than a tie-break.
